editorial.notes: The invocation that closes the prayers of Leo XIII. The Enchiridion Indulgentiarum (1952, n. 675, p. 521) prints it once, as an addition said three times (Praeterea, si addatur ter) with its own indulgence, citing the Sacred Congregation of Indulgences, 17 June 1904, and the Apostolic Penitentiary, 18 March 1932. Five words, and it is said three times — which this edition states in the reader's introduction rather than printing three identical pairs. Witness do prints all three pairs; its literal selection is the first pair, pinned lines 410 and 411 of the Mass Ordo. The answer (s02) is said by all: the Enchiridion Indulgentiarum (1952, n. 675) grants its indulgence to the faithful who say these prayers simul cum sacerdote (p. 521); s01 carries no speaker. COR at w001 is nominative in the function of address, as AGNUS is in the Agnus Dei: the form is a neuter one that would not show the difference anyway, and this edition marks the case the analyzers head. IESU at w002 is genitive — one of the four cases this Greek-Latin name spells alike, and the only one the sense allows here.

source.method: Collated against the witnesses below: witness do, a derived literal selection from the pinned digital Divinum Officium Mass Ordo with no independent transmission, and witness handmissal-tlm, a hand-missal page fetched on 2026-08-07 whose copy is not archived with this edition. Zero substantive divergence, and the orthography each witness declares.
